notes.source: ACS 5-year tables B01001 (Sex by Age) and B09001 (Population Under 18 Years by Age), read by acs_small.py
notes.bands: Five-year bands from B01001, whose own groups are added where they are narrower (15-17 and 18-19; 20, 21 and 22-24; 60-61 and 62-64; 65-66 and 67-69). Published for the municipios only: below them the margin is above 30% of the estimate for 89% or more of the barrios and 95% or more of the census tracts (2020-2024).
notes.under_5: Under 3 and 3-4 come from B09001, which counts children in households only; the band 0 to 4 (B01001) also counts the few in group quarters, so under 3 plus 3-4 can be a little below it.
notes.below_the_municipio: Barrios and census tracts get the age groups whose share is flagged less reliable (margin above 30% of the estimate) for under half of the barrios in 2020-2024: 18 to 44 (39%), 45 to 64 (31%), 65 and over (36%), and under 18 (70%), which the observatory has published since 2026-10-06. 5 to 17 (79%), 18 to 24 (89%), 25 to 44 (53%), under 3 and 3 to 4 (99% or more) are left out.
notes.margins: 90% margins of error by the Census Bureau's formulas: a sum adds its cells' margins in quadrature; a share uses the proportion formula over all people. Where the Census Bureau controls a cell to its own estimates it prints no margin; such a cell adds none, and a count made only of such cells has no margin (it is not exact). A share of 100% has no margin.
notes.sum: In each area the five-year bands add up to all people (B01001_001), and so do under 5, 5-17, 18-24, 25-44, 45-64 and 65+; and under 18, 18-44, 45-64 and 65+.
